sections.title: Introduction
sections.text:
Welcome. Today we come to the very center of the Christian faith: the death and resurrection of Jesus. All four Gospels slow down when they reach this part of the story, spending chapter after chapter on just a few days. The apostle Paul called it the message he delivered “first of all”: that Christ died for our sins, that He was buried, and that He rose again the third day.

This is a hard story in some places, because it tells of real suffering. But it ends with the greatest good news ever announced. As you listen, remember that Jesus went through all of this willingly, and that He did it for you.

sections.title: The Story, Part 1
sections.text:
About seven hundred years before Jesus, the prophet Isaiah wrote about a servant of God who would suffer for others. Isaiah chapter fifty-three, verse five: “But he was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities: the chastisement of our peace was upon him; and with his stripes we are healed.”

On the night before He died, Jesus ate the Passover meal with His twelve disciples. He took bread, gave thanks, broke it, and said, “Take, eat; this is my body.” Then He took the cup and said, “this is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many for the remission of sins.” Christians still remember this meal today in communion, the Lord's Supper.

But one of the twelve, Judas Iscariot, had already gone to the chief priests and agreed to betray Jesus for thirty pieces of silver. And Jesus told Peter, who insisted he would never leave Him, that before the rooster crowed that very night, Peter would deny Him three times.

After supper, Jesus went with His disciples to a garden called Gethsemane. There, in deep sorrow, He prayed, “O my Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me: nevertheless not as I will, but as thou wilt.” Then Judas arrived with a crowd carrying swords and clubs, and he betrayed Jesus with a kiss. The disciples ran away.

Jesus was taken to the high priest and the council. They looked for false witnesses against Him. Meanwhile, Peter sat outside in the courtyard. Three times people recognized him as one of Jesus' followers, and three times he denied it. Then the rooster crowed. Peter remembered Jesus' words, went out, and wept bitterly.

sections.title: The Story, Part 2
sections.text:
In the morning, Jesus was brought to the Roman governor, Pontius Pilate. Pilate questioned Him and said, “I find no fault in this man.” But the crowd, stirred up by the chief priests, shouted, crucify Him! Pilate wanted to please the people, so he released a prisoner named Barabbas and handed Jesus over to be crucified. The soldiers beat Him, put a crown of thorns on His head, and mocked Him.

They led Him to a place called Calvary, and there they crucified Him between two criminals. Even then, Jesus prayed for the people who were killing Him. Luke chapter twenty-three, verse thirty-four: “Then said Jesus, Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do.” One of the criminals mocked Him, but the other asked, “Lord, remember me when thou comest into thy kingdom.” Jesus answered, “To day shalt thou be with me in paradise.”

From noon until three in the afternoon, darkness covered the land. Near the end, John chapter nineteen, verse thirty tells us: “When Jesus therefore had received the vinegar, he said, It is finished: and he bowed his head, and gave up the ghost.” It is finished — the work He came to do was complete. The veil of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom. And a Roman centurion who watched it all said, “Truly this was the Son of God.”

A rich man named Joseph of Arimathaea asked Pilate for the body. He wrapped it in clean linen and laid it in his own new tomb, cut out of rock, and rolled a great stone over the door. The tomb was sealed, and soldiers stood guard.

Early on the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene and other women came to the tomb with spices. There had been a great earthquake, and an angel of the Lord had rolled back the stone and was sitting on it. The guards shook with fear. The angel said to the women, “Fear not ye: for I know that ye seek Jesus, which was crucified.” Then came the words that changed everything. Matthew chapter twenty-eight, verse six: “He is not here: for he is risen, as he said. Come, see the place where the Lord lay.”

Jesus appeared to Mary Magdalene in the garden and called her by name. He appeared to the disciples, showing them His hands and His side. He even met Peter by the sea and restored him, asking him three times, do you love me? — once for each denial. Over forty days, He appeared to many people, and then He ascended into heaven.

sections.title: The Lesson
sections.text:
What does the cross and the empty tomb mean for us?

First, the cross shows how serious our sin is, and how great God's love is. Jesus was wounded for our transgressions. He took the punishment we deserved. As Paul wrote, Christ died for our sins. We could never pay that debt, so He paid it for us.

Second, forgiveness is offered to everyone. Jesus forgave the soldiers who crucified Him. He promised paradise to a dying criminal who simply asked to be remembered. He restored Peter after his worst failure. No one is too far gone.

Third, the resurrection proves that it worked. If Jesus had stayed in the tomb, the cross would have been the end of the story. But He is risen. Death has been defeated, and everyone who trusts in Him will be raised to new life too.

And finally, because Jesus lives, we have hope. Whatever sorrow, sickness, failure, or loss you are facing, it does not get the last word. Easter morning does.

sections.title: Prayer and Reflection
sections.text:
Take a quiet moment to thank Jesus for the cross. If you have never put your trust in Him, you can do it right now, simply by telling Him that you believe He died for your sins and rose again, and that you want to follow Him.

Let's pray. Lord Jesus, thank You for being wounded for my transgressions. Thank You for Your words, Father, forgive them. Thank You that You are risen, just as You said. I put my trust in You. Help me live each day in the hope of Your resurrection. In Your name, Amen.

Thank you for listening. Next time, we'll follow the apostle Paul on his journeys to spread this good news to the world.
